name: MathlibAnnex.IsometryEquiv.map_midpoint_of_mem_ball
title: Midpoint preservation on a quarter ball

content.display_title: Midpoint preservation on a quarter ball
content.one_sentence_role: Supplies both lens inclusions from matching ambient balls.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $E,F$ be real normed spaces, $S\subseteq E$, $T\subseteq F$, and $f:S\to T$ a bijective isometry. Let $c\in S$ and $R>0$ satisfy $B(c,R)\subseteq S$ and $B(f(c),R)\subseteq T$, where $B(c,R)=\{z:\|z-c\|<R\}$. For $x,y\in S\cap B(c,R/4)$, $$f\!\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\frac{f(x)+f(y)}2.$$
content.assumptions: Both ambient open-ball inclusions, positivity of $R$, and membership of both $x,y$ in the quarter ball are required. The sets $S,T$ need not themselves be open or convex.
content.conclusion: The midpoint belongs to $S$, and the same isometry preserves that midpoint.
content.proof_summary: Use radius $R/2$ for the source and target lenses. The quarter-ball bounds leave enough room for both lenses inside the given radius-$R$ balls.
proof_steps: The triangle inequality gives $\|x-y\|\le\|x-c\|+\|y-c\|<R/2$, so $\|x-y\|/2<R/4<R/2$. Also $$\left\|\frac{x+y}{2}-c\right\|\le\frac{\|x-c\|+\|y-c\|}{2}<R/4<R.$$ Thus the midpoint is a valid argument of $f$.
For $z\in \Lambda_{R/2}(x,y)=\overline B(x,R/2)\cap\overline B(y,R/2)$, $$\|z-c\|\le\|z-x\|+\|x-c\|<R/2+R/4<R.$$ Hence this entire lens lies in $B(c,R)\subseteq S$.

Isometry gives $\|f(x)-f(c)\|=\|x-c\|<R/4$. If $w\in \Lambda_{R/2}(f(x),f(y))$, then $$\|w-f(c)\|\le\|w-f(x)\|+\|f(x)-f(c)\|<R/2+R/4<R.$$ The target ball assumption now puts the entire target lens in $T$.

Apply [Midpoint preservation under two lens inclusions](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Affine/IsometryExtension/Local.lean#L120-L135) to this $f$, the points $x,y$, and the radius $R/2$. Step 1 supplies its half-distance bound, and Steps 2–3 supply its two inclusions. Its output is exactly the claimed midpoint equation.
